risk_if_not_implemented: Without Insecure Ports, Protocols & Services, applications may be built and deployed with exploitable design and coding weaknesses that adversaries can leverage. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Exposure from Unaddressed Vulnerabilities (R-EX-6), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Requirements Definition
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to proactively govern Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) by:
(1) Defining technical security, compliance and resilience requirements; and
(2) Performing a criticality analysis at predefined decision points in the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
compensating_control_1.justification: Security, Compliance & Resilience Requirements Definition (PRM-09) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Insecure Ports, Protocols & Services (TDA-11.2) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Security Requirements
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to design, develop and produce Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in such a way that risk-based technical and functional specifications ensure Minimum Viable Product (MVP) criteria establish an appropriate level of security and resiliency based on applicable risks and threats.
compensating_control_2.justification: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Security Requirements (TDA-11.1) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Insecure Ports, Protocols & Services (TDA-11.2) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
